item.description: The next_token function signature is incorrect. It requires a second parameter 'i' but is being called without it in many test cases, causing TypeError exceptions. This is a fundamental interface mismatch.
item.contract: The next_token function must accept two parameters: 'text' (bytes) and 'i' (int). The 'i' parameter represents the starting index for tokenization. When called from test cases, it should properly handle the index parameter.
item.acceptance: tests/test_tokenization.py::Tokenization::test_boolean_true, tests/test_tokenization.py::Tokenization::test_boolean_false, tests/test_tokenization.py::Tokenization::test_integer, etc. (all tokenization tests failing with missing 'i' argument)

item.description: The serialize function produces incorrectly formatted output for arrays. It's missing proper spacing around elements and brackets, causing test failures.
item.contract: The serialize function must produce properly formatted byte strings for arrays with correct spacing: b'[ /abc 123 ]' instead of b'[/abc 123]'

item.description: Integer conversion logic in parsing tests fails when trying to convert malformed byte strings like b'123%d' to integers, causing ValueError exceptions.
item.contract: The parsing logic must properly handle conversion of numeric values from byte strings to integers/floats without raising ValueError exceptions.

item.description: String parsing logic in next_token function is incomplete, particularly for handling literal and hexadecimal strings. This leads to improper tokenization of string literals.
item.contract: The next_token function must properly recognize and tokenize literal strings (enclosed in parentheses) and hexadecimal strings (enclosed in angle brackets) with correct boundaries.
